chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Mihran ibn Muhammad, from a man, from Sa'd al-Iskaf, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever drinks an intoxicant, his prayer will not be accepted from him for forty days; and if he repeats, Allah will quench him from the essence of Khabal. He said, I said, 'And what is the essence of Khabal?' So he said, 'Water that comes out from the private parts of the adulteresses.'
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence for a person's prayer if they drink an intoxicant?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the specific legal consequence of consuming intoxicants, linking the physical act to a forty-day rejection of prayer and a divine punishment of drinking from 'Khabal'. The Imam’s explanation of 'Khabal' as water from the private parts of adulteresses provides a unique metaphysical or physiological dimension to the impurity associated with major sins, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interconnectedness of ritual purity and spiritual state. This narration is frequently cited in fiqh discussions regarding the duration of salat rejection for habitual versus occasional drinkers, underscoring the gravity of khamr in Shia jurisprudence.
